expectations.text: Refuses to output slide files or a deck export, and states that slide files come later from a deck tool
expectations.evidence: "'Export straight into Google Slides' — not building the deck. The skill refuses this outright... What you get below is the skeleton... which you paste into Slides yourself once it's survived a timed run, not before."

expectations.text: Rejects the 22-slides-for-22-minutes rule and states that slide count is an outcome, never a target
expectations.evidence: "'22 slides, one per minute' — not applying this. The skill's own craft rules are explicit: 'There is no slides-per-minute rule... let the count fall out of [what each slide has to accomplish].'"

expectations.text: Gives the range slide counts legitimately take as a counter-example - a story-led talk on a handful of slides, a dense technical talk running around a hundred in thirty minutes
expectations.evidence: No such range or counter-example appears anywhere in the transcript; only a specific prediction for this talk ('I'd bet it lands around 14-16') is given.

expectations.text: Produces instead an ordered list of what each slide must accomplish
expectations.evidence: The 14-item slide skeleton lists each slide's title/purpose in order, e.g. "5. MARKER (Pillar 1) — Title: 'Three things we tried that didn't work' · List the 3 dead ends by name only, no detail yet".

expectations.text: Requires each slide title to be written as the takeaway sentence rather than a topic label, and shows a worked contrast between the two
expectations.evidence: Titles are written as takeaway sentences throughout (e.g. 'We were solving the wrong layer'), but no worked contrast against a topic-label version is shown anywhere.

expectations.text: Requires one idea per slide, and splitting any slide that carries more than one

expectations.text: Requires that nothing appear on screen the speaker is not about to say, with the reason that the audience reads faster than the speaker talks
expectations.evidence: No such requirement or reasoning about reading speed appears anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Gives every section a marker slide so a listener who drifted has a visible way back into the talk
